suggestion.title: Rust Binary Execution on Routers and Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Rebuilds in Rust to Hijack Routers'—Rust binaries are the delivery and execution mechanism. Pipeline generated zero UC despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of Rust-compiled binaries or Rust runtime processes on networking infrastructure (routers, switches, gateways) and servers where Rust is not expected. Monitor for file names, PE sections, or signatures consistent with RustDuck malware.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Communication from Infrastructure Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Botnets fundamentally require command-and-control. Article describes hijacking for DDoS operation but pipeline extracted zero C2 detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish outbound connection baselines for routers and servers (typically absent or management-only). Alert on regular beaconing patterns, DNS requests to unknown domains, HTTP POST activity, or encrypted tunnels from compromised infrastructure. Correlate with botnet C2 reputation feeds.

suggestion.title: DDoS Traffic Generation from Compromised Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states purpose is 'for DDoS'—yet pipeline generated no detection use case for outbound attack traffic. This is the impact phase and highest-severity signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal egress traffic volume, sustained connections to external targets on non-standard ports, and traffic patterns consistent with HTTP floods, UDP floods, or SYN floods. Alert when routers/servers initiate simultaneous attacks to multiple destinations.

suggestion.title: Router and Server Initial Compromise via Public-Facing Services
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'hijacking' routers and servers—implying an initial access exploit or credential compromise not covered in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation attempts or unusual login activity targeting router management interfaces (HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, Telnet, SNMP). Alert on failed login spikes, credential spraying, or successful logins from external IPs. Correlate with known router/server CVEs.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Startup/Boot Mechanisms on Compromised Devices
suggestion.rationale: Botnets require reboot persistence. Article implies sustained compromise but pipeline generated no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cron jobs, systemd timers, startup scripts, and registry run keys on routers and servers for suspicious entries. Alert on new unsigned binaries or scripts added to autostart locations, especially those calling Rust interpreters or binary payloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Scanning and Reconnaissance from Botnet Nodes
suggestion.rationale: Operator mentions 'hijack routers and servers' (plural)—suggesting network scanning post-compromise. Pipeline missed discovery-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scanning, ping sweeps, service enumeration, or SMB/SSH probing originating from compromised routers and servers—anomalous for infrastructure endpoints. Flag ICMP activity, TCP/UDP SYN floods to internal ranges, or multiple connection attempts to known vulnerable ports.

suggestion.title: Langflow RCE Exploitation Attempt (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Langflow RCE Exploited.' Pipeline missed the primary attack vector entirely. Exposed Langflow endpoints are the explicit entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Langflow API endpoints (/api/v1/*, /run/*, /config) for POST payloads containing code injection, eval(), exec(), or subprocess patterns. Flag 401/403→200 response sequences indicating auth bypass or exploitation. Correlate with known Langflow CVE payloads.

suggestion.title: Monero Miner Binary Execution Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Deploy Monero Miner.' No process-based detection for miner execution despite this being the post-exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on spawning of xmrig, xmr-stak, cpuminer, or obfuscated process names from /tmp, /var/tmp, or %appdata% directories following Langflow service activity. Monitor parent-child relationships: Langflow→shell→miner_binary.

suggestion.title: Mining Pool C2 Communication Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Monero miner requires persistent outbound connections to mining pools; no network detection layer for mining traffic in pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained outbound TCP on ports 3333, 5555, 14444, 45560 (Monero pool defaults) or DNS queries resolving to known mining pools (supportxmr.com, pool.monero, minergate.com). Flag high-volume failed connection attempts indicating stratum protocol handshakes.

suggestion.title: Resource Hijacking – Anomalous CPU Consumption
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Deploy Monero Miner on Exposed AI App Endpoints.' Cryptomining causes sustained resource exhaustion; no performance anomaly detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CPU utilization spike >70% sustained >10 minutes from baseline on Langflow host, especially multi-threaded consumption matching miner thread count. Correlate with network outbound to mining pools and absence of legitimate workload.

suggestion.title: Langflow Container Breakout – Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: RCE execution likely originates in unprivileged Langflow container/app context; miner deployment implies privilege escalation or lateral pivot to host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for elevation of privilege from Langflow app user to root/SYSTEM, or appearance of processes in protected directories (/usr/bin, C:\Windows\System32) spawned by Langflow service account. Check for sudo/UAC bypass attempts in logs.

suggestion.title: Exposed Langflow Service Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exposed AI App Endpoints.' Attacker-side recon for vulnerable Langflow instances not detected; no discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts or HTTP HEAD/OPTIONS requests to Langflow /health, /config, or /version endpoints from external IPs. Alert on scanning patterns typical of shodan/censys queries targeting AI app ports (8000, 8080).

suggestion.title: Detect Parallel C2 Channels in Single Intrusion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'parallel threat activity' and 'dual threat actors'—this requires UC detecting multiple command-and-control frameworks or C2 communication patterns from different actors operating simultaneously within the same compromise. Standard single-actor C2 detection will miss the second actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network egress to multiple distinct C2 infrastructure (different ASNs, certificate issuers, or behavioral signatures) from the same host or user session. Look for command-and-control patterns that don't cluster together in timing, protocol, or endpoint behavior—an indicator that two independent operators are working the same infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Activity Divergence by Tool Set
suggestion.rationale: Two actors operating in parallel suggests different tooling, lateral movement patterns, and objectives. The article's premise of 'uncovering parallel threat activity' implies tools or behaviors that initially appeared as a single actor but diverge under close inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag lateral movement where the source/target account combinations, protocols, and timing patterns suggest two distinct operators. Example: Actor A uses Pass-the-Hash via NTLM every 30 minutes; Actor B uses RDP with interactive login and different scheduling. Cluster by tool signature and break detection to identify multiple actors.

suggestion.title: Competing Persistence Mechanisms in Same Host
suggestion.rationale: With two actors in one intrusion, persistence mechanisms may conflict or diverge. Article title 'uncovering parallel' suggests discovery required forensic analysis—implying initially-hidden or competing persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple scheduled tasks, registry Run keys, or service installations from different source processes within a short timeframe (hours to days). Two actors separately establishing persistence will use different accounts, tools, and timing. Cluster persistence artifacts by tool provenance and creation source.

suggestion.title: Multi-Actor Privilege Escalation Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Two actors in parallel likely trigger multiple privilege escalation attempts or use cases. The article's focus on 'uncovering' suggests they initially appeared as one attack chain but were actually two.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate privilege escalation attempts by distinct tool chains (e.g., one using PrintSpooler exploitation, another using NtlmRelayToEWS). Two actors will use different attack vectors and timing—flag escalation sequences with temporal gaps or diverging payload characteristics.

suggestion.title: Detect Shadowing / Objective Divergence Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'blended tactics' that 'conceal attacks'—two actors working the same box may shadow each other or pursue conflicting objectives (one exfil, one ransomware prep). This requires behavioral divergence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify file collection by two actors: one targeting finance/IP (Actor A tools), another targeting HR/employee data (Actor B tools). Timeline overlap + divergent file access patterns + different user contexts = multi-actor indicator.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Instance Exposed to Internet (Asset-Exposure Hunt)
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes T1190 exploitation against public-facing application and recommends asset-exposure hunt per template. Exposed Splunk instances are the prerequisite for this CVE to be exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8000, 8089, 8191) reachable from untrusted networks. Cross-reference external asset inventories (Shodan, Censys, your cloud asset tags) against internal Splunk fleet. Flag any instance without WAF, reverse proxy, or TLS inspection in front.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access to Critical Function
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the attack path and should be directly hunted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar (internal port, typically 5432 or mapped via sidecar config) lacking valid auth credentials or session tokens. Alert on CREATE/DROP/TRUNCATE/WRITE operations from unexpected sources. Splunk Enterprise audit logs should show critical function invocation by unauthenticated user.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is the post-compromise activity chain. File operations via sidecar are anomalous and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/deletion events that correlate with Splunk sidecar process or PostgreSQL service user (splunk, postgres). Baseline expected file paths; flag modifications to system directories, config files, or Splunk installation directories. Enrich with network context to confirm no legitimate sidecar-to-sidecar communication.

suggestion.title: Scanner Blindness to Patch Lag (CVE-2026-20253 Deployed-But-Unpatched)
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'patch lag is the silent killer' and 'worth one quick check across your fleet'—vulnerability scanners alone miss instances running vulnerable code despite reporting patches. Direct version verification required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Beyond scanner matches, query Splunk REST API (`/services/server/info`) on each instance to confirm actual running version. Flag instances where scanner reports patched but API returns version ≤8.2.11 (or applicable vulnerable range). Prioritize instances with 10+ day patch lag.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Exposed PostgreSQL Sidecar Port
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires discovery of the sidecar endpoint. Reconnaissance traffic (port scans, service fingerprinting) against sidecar ports precedes successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for external sources probing PostgreSQL port (5432) or mapped sidecar ports against Splunk infrastructure. Look for SYN/SYN-ACK patterns without successful auth handshake. Correlate with subsequent CVE-2026-20253 exploitation attempts (file ops, auth bypass attempts) to confirm attack chain.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Critical-Function HTTP Calls Without Auth Header
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: missing authentication for critical function. Direct HTTP/API calls to protected endpoints lack expected Authorization headers or session cookies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET requests to Splunk critical endpoints (file manipulation APIs, deployment endpoints) that lack `Authorization` header or valid session cookie. Flag 200-OK responses to file-write endpoints from sources that should require auth. Correlate with subsequent file system modifications.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise - Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Unauthenticated access is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic to Splunk Enterprise hosts for requests to the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint lacking authentication (missing or invalid auth headers, missing session tokens, or direct unauthenticated socket connections). Baseline legitimate sidecar traffic and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise - Arbitrary File Truncation/Creation via CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File operations are the exploitation payload and observable impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events originating from the PostgreSQL sidecar process or correlating with unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access. Focus on Splunk configuration directories, system files, and unexpected write operations outside the sidecar's normal scope.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 - Unpatched Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited' and federal patch due date is 2026-06-21. Asset inventory is the foundational detection for known-exploited vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Splunk Enterprise deployments and cross-reference against known vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-20253. Prioritize instances with the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint exposed to untrusted networks, accessible via public IPs, or behind weak/missing authentication.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise - PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Port/Path Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Prior to exploitation, attackers must discover the sidecar endpoint. Article implies network accessibility, making reconnaissance observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for port scans, HTTP OPTIONS probes, or failed connection attempts targeting PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or variants) on Splunk hosts. Look for scanning patterns followed by successful exploitation (successful file operations).

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise - Critical Configuration File Tampering via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Truncation of Splunk configuration files (props.conf, transforms.conf, inputs.conf, etc.) would cause operational damage and indicate post-exploitation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk configuration directories for file truncation or unexpected modifications outside of change-control processes. Correlate with PostgreSQL sidecar activity or unauthenticated endpoint access. Alert on any loss of file content in critical app directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — core initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk internal service endpoints (PostgreSQL sidecar, /_internal/*, /api/*) that return 200/201 without prior 401/403 or without valid session token. Flag unauthenticated IPs with successful requests to admin/sidecar paths.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — post-exploitation impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Splunk sidecar process file operations (FileCreate, FileDelete) with recent unauthenticated HTTP POST/PUT requests to sidecar endpoints. Alert on file modifications to Splunk config, data, or system directories initiated without valid admin authentication.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Public-Facing Instance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — requires baseline inventory of Internet-accessible Splunk Enterprise deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Splunk Enterprise instances with public DNS/certificate records. Cross-reference against internal asset inventory to identify instances accessible from untrusted networks. Correlate exposure timeline with CVE-2026-20253 publication (2026-06-18) and CISA KEV addition.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover sidecar endpoint before exploitation — 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' implies reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk endpoints containing 'postgresql', 'sidecar', 'service', or unusual admin API paths (/_internal/*, /api/postgresql*). Alert on high-volume 404 responses followed by successful 200 responses to the same endpoint path.

suggestion.title: Splunk Patch Status Verification for CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes checking patch status even if scanners report 'not vulnerable' due to 'patch lag' — compliance/verification hunt against scanner reports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for Splunk Enterprise; cross-reference 'patched' status against actual running version from asset inventory or /rest/server/info endpoint. Alert if scanner report mismatches reality or if patch date is older than CVE-2026-20253 publication date but version still unpatched.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Port/Endpoint Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Sidecar endpoint must be network-accessible to unauthenticated attacker — 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' implies specific listening port or HTTP route exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar listening ports (default: 8000, 8088, 8089 or custom) exposed to untrusted networks. Alert on external traffic to sidecar service endpoints. Cross-reference Shodan/Internet scans for exposed Splunk + PostgreSQL combinations matching known sidecar architectures.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active exploitation of exposed Splunk instances. Article describes vulnerability in 'Splunk Enterprise' product with no mention of internal-only deployments. Requires immediate external-facing asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8000, 8089, 9997, 8191) accepting inbound connections from non-private IP ranges. Cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2026-20253. Prioritize instances reachable on management ports (8089).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation mechanism requiring immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-creation and file-truncation events initiated by Splunk processes or from unauthenticated service accounts. Look for mass file deletions or creation of files in unexpected Splunk directories without corresponding authenticated API calls. Correlate with external IP connections to sidecar ports.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation / Truncation by Splunk
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is impact-level detection. Unusual file operations by Splunk processes or in Splunk-controlled paths indicate exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/deletion in Splunk installation directories, configuration paths, or index locations without corresponding legitimate Splunk processes. Flag mass truncation events. Baseline normal Splunk file operations and alert on deviations from authenticated admin or backup processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch-due date of 2026-06-21. Pipeline must correlate vulnerability scanner output against Splunk Enterprise inventory to identify unpatched systems at active risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Splunk Enterprise version/build against known-vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-20253. Prioritize systems with CVE present AND internet-facing. Flag any unpatched instances as P0 for immediate remediation. Correlate with firewall/proxy logs for exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation vector; no detection logic provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking authentication headers (no Authorization, session token, or API key). Correlate with Splunk access logs showing requests with no user context. Alert on anomalous traffic volume or previously unseen endpoint paths to sidecar ports.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise: Arbitrary File Manipulation via Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files' as the attack outcome. No file-activity detection generated despite this being the direct impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file write, create, or truncate operations initiated by Splunk sidecar processes targeting paths outside Splunk's standard directory structure (var/lib/splunk, etc.). Correlate with absence of prior authentication logs for that process user. High-confidence signal when combined with PostgreSQL endpoint access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance precedes exploitation. Attackers must discover sidecar endpoint availability before exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or connection attempts to known Splunk sidecar service ports (consult vendor docs for version-specific defaults) from external IPs or unexpected internal subnets. Flag sequences of failed connections followed by successful unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Public PoC/Scanner Signatures
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active wild exploitation; public scanners and PoC tools exist. Vendor-published scanner signatures or known request patterns are immediate high-confidence indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement signature detection for HTTP request patterns associated with published CVE-2026-20253 PoC tools: specific User-Agent strings, malformed or probing request paths to sidecar endpoints, or payload structures documented in vendor security advisories. Cross-reference with CISA advisory for IoC updates.

suggestion.title: Malicious Go Package Installation (botdb-go/bolt v1.3.1)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the malicious package 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' version '1.3.1' released November 2021. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite this being the definitive supply-chain indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build/package manager logs (go.mod, go.sum, pip, npm equivalents) for installation of package 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' version 1.3.1. Cross-reference against known-good package signatures from official registry checksums. Alert on any cached or permanently-stored references to this coordinate in module proxy mirrors post-January-2025.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Package Name Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article states the malicious package 'botdb-go/bolt' mimicked legitimate 'boltdb/bolt'. Pipeline should flag typosquatting detection across package names—'A big flaw in the supply chain ecosystem.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Levenshtein-distance similarity (≤3 edits) between installed package names and known-legitimate packages in high-volume usage. Flag installs of 'botdb-go/*' variants against 'boltdb/*' baseline. Cross-reference against typosquatting feeds (Snyk, Socket, etc.).

suggestion.title: Remote Command Execution via Backdoored Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This backdoor allows hackers to remotely control infected computers through a server that sends them commands.' Pipeline missed C2 detection for the actual exploit mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile network traffic from systems with 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt' in dependency tree for anomalous outbound C2 patterns (beaconing, command-response, etc.). Baseline should establish Go process group network behavior; alert on deviations. Monitor for DNS queries to C2 infrastructure if identified in malware analysis reports.

suggestion.title: Module Cache Persistence - Long-Lived Malicious Module
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Go Module Mirror's indefinite caching of modules kicked in, and that cached the backdored module.' This describes a persistence mechanism unique to the Go ecosystem and warrant detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Go module cache directories ($GOPATH/pkg/mod) for files matching coordinate 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt@v1.3.1*'. Alert if cache timestamp predates January 30, 2025 (discovery date). Track module proxy requests for persistence of reverted packages—if removed upstream but still served locally, escalate.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Dependency Update to Compromised Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Now we wish to update our systems to the latest dependencies, which led developers to update the version that stayed in the system for 3 years.' Developers pulling latest versions triggered the incident.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag 'go get -u' or equivalent bulk-dependency-update commands immediately preceding or concurrent with installation of 'github.com/botdb-go/bolt'. Correlate with build artifacts and deployment actions. Alert if update pulls from fork/typosquat variant instead of canonical repository.

suggestion.title: Known Malicious Go Module from Go Vulnerability Database
suggestion.rationale: Article references Snyk and Go vulnerability database entries (GO-2025-3451, SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841). Pipeline should integrate these CVE/advisory indices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Consume Go vulnerability database (pkg.go.dev/vuln) and Snyk advisory feeds to flag installations of GO-2025-3451 and SNYK-GOLANG-GITHUBCOMBOLTDBGOBOLT-868841. Cross-check all go.mod/go.sum files in environment against these indices. Alert on any transitive dependencies that pull affected module.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Splunk Enterprise Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Splunk Enterprise, provides CVE-2026-20253, and references canonical asset-exposure hunt: 'Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure.' Federal patch due-date is 2026-06-21; any unpatched instance is a critical control gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for all Splunk Enterprise instances. Flag any running version that does not have the patch for CVE-2026-20253 applied. Cross-reference with network exposure data; prioritize internet-facing instances. Alert for all unpatched instances, with federal due-date 2026-06-21 as enforcement boundary.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' The missing authentication is the exploit path; detect access to this endpoint without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs for requests to the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint without authentication headers or with invalid/missing credentials. Correlate with network IDS alerts on sidecar service ports (typically internal, but flag if externally routable). Alert on any unauthenticated endpoint access attempt with urgency proportional to external reachability.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Process
suggestion.rationale: Article impact statement: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detect filesystem manifestation of this exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and truncation events on Splunk Enterprise hosts, particularly outside normal Splunk directories. Flag any file operations initiated through postgresql or sidecar processes, or triggered shortly after unauthenticated endpoint access. Correlate filesystem events with network logs showing sidecar endpoint connections.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration or State File Tampering via Unauthorized Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: File truncation capability implies potential destruction of Splunk configuration, state, or audit logs. Detect unauthorized modification of Splunk-critical files as secondary exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk internal audit logs for unexpected changes to authentication policies, configuration objects, or index definitions. Correlate with file integrity monitoring alerts on SPLUNK_HOME/etc and SPLUNK_HOME/var directories. Alert on truncation or deletion of audit logs, configuration files, or cluster state files following detection of sidecar endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'public-facing application' status and KEV designation (active exploitation). Article body instructs 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>.' Any externally accessible Splunk instance is immediately at risk for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise instances (default ports 8000, 8089) accepting inbound connections from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Prioritize instances where patch deployment lags >7 days past federal due date (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Sidecar access is the necessary exploitation step; unauthorized connection attempts are direct detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports from external or non-service-account contexts with failed authentication. Monitor Splunk audit logs for unauthorized access to /_internal or sidecar-specific endpoints. Baseline should show zero external sidecar traffic.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Create/Truncate Operations via Splunk Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation impact explicitly stated: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' File operations are the destructive payload; this is a separate detection angle from access detection. Article specifies this as the direct capability granted by the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation with parent process being Splunk sidecar/PostgreSQL and executing principal being the Splunk service account, particularly on system files, config directories, or auth stores outside change-control windows. Flag rapid sequential file operations on critical binaries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Sidecar Endpoint Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation. Article identifies sidecar endpoint as specific attack surface. Direct exploitation detection will catch in-flight attacks targeting this vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk internal endpoints (/_internal, /_kvstore, /admin paths) from unauthenticated sessions or external IPs. Look for payloads with file path traversal patterns, PostgreSQL command keywords (CREATE, TRUNCATE), or sidecar-specific parameter names. Alert on any 20x response to these endpoints from external sources.

suggestion.title: Splunk Audit Log Truncation or Authentication Bypass Evidence Destruction
suggestion.rationale: Article's explicit reference to 'truncate arbitrary files' capability enables evidence destruction. Adversary would likely disable or wipe audit trails to hide exploitation. This defense-evasion step should be detectable via log integrity monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on truncation or deletion of Splunk audit.log, authentication logs, or audit.conf modifications disabling audit logging. Correlate with sidecar access events. Maintain cryptographically-signed, out-of-band audit backups to detect local tampering.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar PostgreSQL Endpoint Unauthenticated Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline produced zero detections for this primary exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints (typically 8091–8099 range) that lack valid authentication tokens or use null/bypass payloads. Baseline legitimate sidecar consumers; flag requests from unexpected source IPs or user-agents. Correlate failed auth attempts followed by successful file manipulation events.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Enterprise Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article names capability: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' No impact-phase detection generated for post-exploitation file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation/truncation events originating from Splunk service accounts or sidecar processes targeting non-standard directories (OS roots, /etc, System32, web roots). Establish baseline of legitimate Splunk file operations; detect anomalous writes to config, data, or log paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Public Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires validation that vulnerable instances are not internet-exposed. Article context: 'currently being exploited in the wild.' No asset-inventory or public-reachability hunt generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise instances listening on public IPs without firewall restrictions.
