Baseline normal Splunk admin traffic and alert on deviations from known service-account patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' File-write IOCs are direct impact indicators; detect fs operations initiated from Splunk service processes that bypass normal ACLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation in sensitive directories (e.g., /etc, /opt/splunk/etc/apps, Windows system32) where the calling process is Splunk Enterprise and the parent process is the PostgreSQL sidecar or a network-facing service. Flag unexpected file extensions (.sh, .bat, .exe) or modifications to configuration files.

suggestion.title: Network Discovery of Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Ports
suggestion.rationale: For CVE-2026-20253 exploitation, attacker must first identify vulnerable Splunk instances. Article implies port-based service discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or enumeration against Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (8191, 9000, 8000, custom) originating from external IPs. Correlate with subsequent auth-bypass attempts to the same destination within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempts in Splunk Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'observed exploited in the wild' (CISA KEV); Splunk logs will record exploitation payloads in access logs or error messages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Splunk access logs and search for HTTP POST/GET requests to /services/server/info or /api/splunk-sidecar-svc endpoints with null/missing auth tokens and payloads attempting to write or delete files. Flag requests with `mkdir`, `rm`, `truncate`, or file paths in query parameters.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Followed by Success
suggestion.rationale: Indicators of auth-bypass exploitation: repeated failed auth attempts immediately followed by privileged file operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences: 3+ failed HTTP 401/403 responses to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint → immediate HTTP 200 response → file creation/deletion in splunkd logs within 10-second window. This pattern suggests successful auth-bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Version Inventory and Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal patch due 2026-06-21. Asset-exposure hunt for vulnerable versions (pre-patch) to ensure compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for Splunk Enterprise instances with version < 9.1.2 or 9.0.x (typical patch boundaries). Cross-reference with network scan data to identify internet-facing Splunk instances. Prioritize instances without network segmentation or WAF protection.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can access 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' without authentication. This is the attack foothold and must be detected as inbound connections to the sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful or repeated connection attempts to the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically :5432 or Splunk internal port) from external/untrusted network ranges without prior authentication handshake. Alert on connection patterns consistent with scanning or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via PostgreSQL Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—detection must flag file operations initiated by PostgreSQL processes with unusual target paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, deletion, or truncation events where the initiating process is PostgreSQL/sidecar and the target path is outside normal data directories (e.g., /tmp, /etc, /var/log). Prioritize Splunk configuration and audit log paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanning Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: As a CISA KEV entry with active in-the-wild exploitation, attackers will actively probe for vulnerable instances. Must detect characteristic reconnaissance signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints returning authentication errors (401, 403) or abnormal response codes, especially in patterns consistent with vulnerability scanning (rapid sequential probes, known scanner User-Agents).

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration File Tampering via Database Query
suggestion.rationale: If attacker truncates or modifies Splunk configuration or audit files via the database endpoint, it could disable logging or escalate privileges. Article's 'truncate arbitrary files' capability enables this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to Splunk critical files (/opt/splunk/etc/*.conf, audit logs) where the triggering process chain includes PostgreSQL sidecar or database query execution. Flag unexpected ownership/permission changes on Splunk binaries or config directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253: Unauthenticated Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the attack surface. Pipeline generated no detections for this exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically port 8191 or internal API paths). Baseline legitimate administrative traffic and alert on deviation. Look for requests originating from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'create arbitrary files'—this is impact. No use case captures post-exploitation file-write activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation events initiated by Splunk Enterprise processes in unexpected directories (outside config/app directories). Correlate file creation with preceding unauthenticated sidecar requests. Alert on files created outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'truncate arbitrary files'—a distinct attack capability. No use case covers file deletion/truncation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncation or zero-byte file writes initiated by Splunk Enterprise or its sidecar processes. Alert on attempts to truncate system files, logs, or security-critical files. Correlate with failed authentication detections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Query Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow depends on sidecar service being accessible and executing file operations. Pipeline missed the database-layer detection angle mentioned by 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL logs within the Splunk sidecar container for CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, or file I/O operations initiated from unexpected callers. Alert on queries that attempt file system operations (COPY TO/FROM) from unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Detect StealC browser credential exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on StealC stealing browser credentials and autofill data; no detection use case exists to flag suspicious access to browser-stored passwords, cookies, or stored payment methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes (particularly rundll32, powershell, cmd, or regsvcs) accessing LSASS or browser credential stores (chrome LocalState, firefox signons.sqlite, DPAPI-protected memory regions). Correlate with immediate network exfiltration to suspicious HTTPS endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect Amadey C2 beaconing and data exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Amadey as delivered via cybercrime MaaS; no use case for detecting Amadey's characteristic C2 communication patterns or the HTTP POST exfiltration of stolen data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS to known Amadey C2 infrastructure or generic POST requests from unusual processes (injected code) containing exfiltrated credential markers (base64-encoded password/token dumps) to attacker-controlled domains.

suggestion.title: Detect infostealer MaaS delivery payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'cybercrime services that deliver' StealC and Amadey; no use case for detecting the delivery stage (emails with malicious attachments, drive-by downloads, typosquat domains) that precedes execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email attachments with names matching known infostealer delivery patterns (invoices, tax documents, fake updates) or downloads from low-reputation/newly-registered domains. Correlate with registry/file modifications typical of installer execution.

suggestion.title: Detect API key and token theft from process memory
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions both StealC and Amadey target 'tokens' and 'stored secrets'; no use case captures detection of process memory scraping for API keys, OAuth tokens, or session cookies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes reading files in .aws, .ssh, .kube, Chrome user data, or Kubernetes config directories, or calling ReadProcessMemory on browser/IDE processes. Flag especially if followed by suspicious file writes or network egress.

suggestion.title: Detect clipboard data exfiltration post-execution
suggestion.rationale: Infostealers like StealC routinely steal clipboard (wallet addresses, authentication codes). No use case detects this collection method or the immediate serialization/upload of clipboard contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process calls to GetClipboardData or clipboard API invocations (WM_GETTEXT on clipboard window) from non-standard processes, especially rundll32 or injected code, immediately followed by compression (7zip, RAR) or Base64 encoding and network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Detect infostealer persistence via registry and startup folders
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'services that deliver' infostealers, implying on-host persistence. No use case for detecting registry run-key modification, startup folder placement, or scheduled task creation by delivered malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to HKCU/HKLM Run, RunOnce, or Policies registries, or file creation in Startup folders, immediately following execution of downloaded/emailed files or following code injection patterns. Correlation: parent process is downloader, child is registry/file writer.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could allow an unauthenticated user... through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Core attack vector requiring immediate detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 or internal Splunk bindings) from external/untrusted sources. Monitor for authentication bypass attempts or unauthenticated command execution against Splunk service endpoints. Correlate with Splunk logs showing critical-function access without valid credentials.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Service Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Post-exploitation impact detection needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, deletion, or truncation events initiated by Splunk service processes with unusual target paths (outside Splunk directories), system-critical locations, or with unexpected timing correlation to suspicious network events on PostgreSQL sidecar ports.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure of Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires PostgreSQL sidecar to be reachable from unauthenticated sources. Article implies network accessibility that should not exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for inbound traffic to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar (port 5432 or internal ranges) originating from external IP space, DMZ, or untrusted segments. Flag PostgreSQL service exposure outside private infrastructure boundaries. Cross-reference with asset inventory for unsecured Splunk instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal patch compliance by 2026-06-21. Must identify and track vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Splunk Enterprise instances for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Match vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Rapid7, Qualys) and Splunk version inventory against advisory. Generate remediation tracking report with federal due-date countdown.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation vector requiring direct monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication headers that return success (200/201). Flag GET/POST to paths like /api/pgsidecar/*, especially those with file operation parameters (truncate, delete, write).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation Initiated by Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File truncation is the destructive impact phase requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file truncation/deletion (O_TRUNC, ftruncate syscalls) by Splunk or PostgreSQL processes. Correlate with prior unauthenticated sidecar access; flag operations outside /var/log/splunk as high-severity exploits.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Audit
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV indicates active exploitation. Article references asset-exposure hunt template for unpatched Splunk Enterprise instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Splunk Enterprise instances (ports 8089, 8000) for unauthenticated endpoint access. Verify authentication enforcement on critical functions; flag instances responding with version banners to unauthenticated requests as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated access to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can access the vulnerability via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the initial foothold and should trigger on HTTP 200 or successful connections to the sidecar port from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar PostgreSQL service endpoints (typically port 9997 or internal service ports) that do not include authentication tokens or valid session cookies. Alert on status 200 responses from external or unusual source IPs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary file creation or truncation via PostgreSQL sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File-system write operations initiated from sidecar service are direct IOCs of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation operations initiated by Splunk sidecar processes (typically splunk-postgres or similar) targeting system directories or sensitive application paths. Flag rapid or bulk file deletions that deviate from baseline.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise asset exposure inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article references a template hunt for asset exposure (CVE-2026-20253 substitute). This is the foundational detection—identify all Splunk instances and their exposure before attackers do.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network logs and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances with exposed sidecar service ports (particularly PostgreSQL 5432 or 9997, or internal service endpoints accessible from external networks). Cross-reference against patch compliance baseline.

suggestion.title: Service port enumeration targeting Splunk sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Prior to file-system exploitation, attackers must first discover or probe the sidecar endpoint. Article describes a service endpoint vulnerability, implying reconnaissance is a precursor step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port scans or connection attempts to Splunk sidecar port ranges (9995–9999, 5432, or internal PostgreSQL ports) from external or non-Splunk-related subnets, especially followed by successful connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk sidecar process anomalies post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once file creation/truncation begins via the sidecar, process behavior diverges from baseline—elevated privileges, unusual parent processes, or file handles on system-critical paths signal active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk sidecar process handle opens and file-write syscalls targeting /etc, /sys, /boot, or application config directories. Baseline sidecar behavior and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Failed or missing authentication logs to Splunk critical endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'missing authentication for critical function.' Absence of auth in logs (vs. failed auth) or direct unauthenticated access to protected endpoints is the threat signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Splunk audit logs for API or service calls to critical functions (file operations, configuration write) with no authentication context or anonymous/default credentials. Flag any successful calls without valid session tokens.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct asset-exposure hunt for exposed Splunk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk instance ports (8000, 8089, 9998) originating from external networks without valid session authentication. Correlate unauthenticated requests to sidecar service endpoints (e.g., /services/sidecar/*, /api/v1/sidecar/*) with network telemetry to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the exploitation phase requiring behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected file-creation or file-truncation events originating from Splunk service processes or PostgreSQL sidecar processes. Alert on writes to system directories, configuration paths, or database files outside scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with published due date 2026-06-21 requires immediate asset inventory. Article states: 'Splunk Enterprise contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Splunk Enterprise assets in your environment with CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability scanner results. Identify instances with sidecar services exposed to unauthenticated network access. Prioritize remediation per federal due-date urgency.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthorized Connection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack surface. Exploitation requires database-level access from unauthenticated sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL audit logs for connection attempts from non-standard sources or without credentials. Flag any DDL operations (CREATE, DROP, ALTER) on Splunk backend tables originating from the sidecar service context initiated by unauthenticated callers.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' — the missing authentication check on critical functions is the attack surface. Detectable via missing or invalid auth tokens on sensitive endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs for requests to critical endpoints (e.g., `/services/`, `/admin/`) missing X-Splunk-Authorization headers or containing invalid/expired tokens. Alert on unauthenticated POSTs to endpoints that normally require authentication.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint File Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — specific attack vector combining auth bypass with file-system impact. Correlate sidecar requests with file-system changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/PUT requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically port 5432 or internal service) followed by file-system creation/truncation events in Splunk directories within 1–5 seconds, especially targeting `/opt/splunk/etc/` or similar configuration paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV (actively exploited). 'Match against your vulnerability scanner' implies standard POC-based signatures should be available. Detection should trigger on known exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints with file-path parameters (e.g., `file=/opt/splunk/...`) originating from external sources or with no authentication context. Correlate with Splunk version detection to scope vulnerable instances (versions prior to patch date 2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Network Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — implies the sidecar is reachable by an unauthenticated user. Misconfiguration or network exposure is the prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Splunk deployments for exposed PostgreSQL sidecar ports reachable from external/untrusted networks. Alert if sidecar responds to unauthenticated connection attempts from sources outside the expected management subnet.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Database Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'truncate arbitrary files' — file destruction via database connector is the specific impact. This should be isolated from creation; truncation implies targeted data loss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-truncation events (not just deletion) in Splunk directories and database paths. Correlate truncations with failed authentication logs or with sidecar endpoint access. Truncation of index metadata or configuration files is high-confidence impact.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—core attack surface: unauthenticated access to exposed sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints (PostgreSQL service port, likely internal) from external/untrusted sources that: (a) return 200–201 without Authorization header, (b) contain SQL-like payloads, (c) originate from IPs not in trusted Splunk admin ranges. Baseline inbound access to PostgreSQL sidecar port and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253: Arbitrary File Truncation/Creation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—critical file manipulation indicator requiring detection on Splunk audit and database logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TRUNCATE or CREATE_FILE operations in PostgreSQL or Splunk audit logs preceded by unauthenticated sidecar endpoint requests. Flag rapid successive TRUNCATE calls (>5 per minute) on critical Splunk config files (props.conf, transforms.conf, outputs.conf). Correlate file operations with preceding unauthorized API requests.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253: Asset Exposure—Vulnerable Instance Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV template mandates asset-exposure hunt; article confirms Splunk Enterprise unpatched before 2026-06-21 federal due date are actively exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch-management logs for Splunk Enterprise instances flagged with CVE-2026-20253. Prioritise assets with internet-facing exposure, last-patched date before 2026-06-21, and running versions below vendor's fixed release. Cross-reference with network egress logs for signs of compromise post-identification.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253: Sidecar Service Misconfiguration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint is exposed without authentication enforcement—configuration audit should detect missing auth controls on sidecar listeners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Splunk Enterprise configuration files and running process arguments for PostgreSQL sidecar service listeners that: (a) bind to 0.0.0.0 or external interfaces, (b) lack authentication middleware, (c) expose service port to untrusted networks. Alert on any changes to sidecar authentication settings post-remediation.

suggestion.title: Malicious PyPI Package Installation (frint/skytext/slogsec)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names trojanized packages on PyPI: 'Once the victim clones a malicious repository, a trojanized package named frint is automatically fetched and installed.' These are actionable, time-sensitive IOCs that warrant immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/python package managers for installation of known-malicious packages (frint, skytext, slogsec, logcrypt.cryptography). Inspect setup.py or requirements.txt in cloned repositories for suspicious dependency chains. Alert on first-time package installations from PyPI with zero historical prevalence or linked to security researcher activity.

suggestion.title: Native Python Extension Loading from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the package pulls a malicious dependency package, skytext, which contains a compiled native Python extension. When the PoC executes, the extension runs automatically.' This is a key evasion tactic hiding malicious code in .so/.pyd files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter loading compiled extensions (.so, .pyd) from temporary directories, package cache (site-packages), or non-standard paths. Cross-reference loaded extension names against PyPI package manifests. Alert on extensions with no public symbol table or loaded immediately post-pip-install.

suggestion.title: Decryption/Code Invocation by Python Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article describes obfuscated payload delivery: 'extension runs automatically and decrypts additional embedded Python code that triggers a downloader.' This defense-evasion step should trigger behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes for crypto library imports (hashlib, cryptography, Crypto) followed by decrypt-like operations on embedded data. Detect loading of base64/hex-encoded payloads followed by exec() or importlib calls. Alert on Python child processes spawned within milliseconds of extension load.

suggestion.title: Mapbox Dataset Access for Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies C2 channel: 'ChocoPoC, from a Mapbox dataset' and 'Mapbox datasets are also abused for data exfiltration.' Direct IOC for C2 beaconing and data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to api.mapbox.com or datasets.mapbox.com from Python processes, especially those spawned by package managers or PoC scripts. Alert on requests with unusual dataset IDs or access patterns. Correlate with browser-data-theft indicators (stolen cookies, passwords in outbound traffic).

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Extraction by Python Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies RAT capability: 'collect browser passwords, cookies, autofill data, and browsing history.' Detect Python accessing browser storage directories and Chrome/Firefox credential databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python processes opening browser credential files (Chrome/profile*/Login Data, Firefox profile sqlite databases, Edge Local State). Detect imports of sqlite3 or keyring libraries by scripts spawned via package installation. Monitor for tar/zip operations on ~/.config/chromium or ~/.mozilla directories.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance via Process and Network Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article lists RAT capabilities: 'enumerate running processes', 'gather shell history from the host', 'collect network configuration.' These discovery activities can be detected in sequence after infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python child processes executing ps, netstat, ifconfig, or uname commands in rapid succession. Monitor for Python libraries querying psutil or subprocess for process lists. Alert on combination: pip install → Python extension load → subprocess calls to system discovery tools → data collection.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Repo-Server Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states flaw in repo-server component allows cluster takeover. No use case was generated to detect exploitation attempts against this public-facing service endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Argo CD repo-server API endpoints (typically /api/v1/repositories, /metrics, or repo-server pod ports 8081-8084) from external sources with unusual payloads, SQL injection patterns, template injection markers, or request paths not consistent with legitimate GitOps operations.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Kubernetes Cluster Admin Role Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'take over Kubernetes clusters'—implying privilege escalation to cluster-admin. No detection for unauthorized RBAC modifications or service account privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of cluster-role-bindings binding non-system service accounts to cluster-admin role, new service accounts with elevated privileges, or unusual kubectl exec/auth commands executed from within Argo CD namespace post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Pod Escape / Host Breakout Detection
suggestion.rationale: Cluster takeover via repo-server likely involves container escape or privilege escalation out of the Argo CD pod. No detection scenario addresses unusual process execution or volume mounts from the compromised pod.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Argo CD repo-server pods for execution of shell interpreters, system binaries (mount, nsenter, chroot), or processes spawning outside expected repo-server application context. Alert on attempts to access host filesystem via /proc or /sys, or binding to privileged ports.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Application/Secret Tampering for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Attackers controlling repo-server can manipulate deployed applications or inject secrets for persistence. No UC covers unauthorized modifications to GitOps config repositories or Argo CD application definitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized commits to Git repositories linked to Argo CD, new Secrets/ConfigMaps created in argocd namespace with suspicious patterns, or application manifests modified to deploy backdoor containers, reverse shells, or additional service accounts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Argo CD Context
suggestion.rationale: Exploiting repo-server provides attackers with Argo CD's cluster credentials and kubeconfig. Pipeline missed detection for lateral movement to other namespaces or clusters managed by Argo CD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected kubectl API calls to clusters other than the Argo CD cluster using Argo CD service account credentials, access to kubeconfig secrets stored in argocd namespace, or sudden enumeration of secrets across multiple namespaces post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 from Argo CD Cluster Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes full cluster takeover; pipeline should have flagged detection of exfiltration or C2 communication originating from the compromised cluster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from Argo CD pods and nodes for connections to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, unusual protocols (DNS tunneling, ICMP, non-standard ports), or patterns consistent with reverse shell or exfiltration traffic.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Phishing and Social Engineering Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names Scattered Spider, a group known for social engineering vectors; pipeline should have mapped initial-access detections for phishing emails, credential-phishing, and impersonation attempts targeting high-value targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with URL shorteners, lookalike domains, or sender spoofing from untrusted external sources. Flag conversation threads building rapport before requesting credentials or sensitive access information.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Credential Enumeration and Targeted Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Group methodology involves testing stolen credentials across multiple systems and cloud services; detection should cover account enumeration and auth anomalies preceding successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid user enumeration (failed user lookups) followed by targeted brute-force or password-spray attempts within short time window. Correlate cloud and on-premises sign-in failures preceding successful authentications.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: SSH Lateral Movement and Interactive Shell Access
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider uses SSH for lateral movement post-compromise; extradition for hacking charges implies investigation uncovered lateral movement activity requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH connections from unusual ASNs or IPs followed by interactive shell spawning (bash, sh, zsh). Alert on shell processes initiated by sshd running as privileged user at off-hours.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Data Collection and Exfiltration Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses extradition for hacking charges; Scattered Spider stages data via clipboard capture, archive compression, and collection of sensitive files before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes accessing clipboard APIs, browser process memory, or SSH key storage. Detect archive creation (tar, 7z, zip) of ~/.ssh, /home/*/Documents, or cloud-sync directories followed by network egress.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Living-off-the-Land and Shell Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Group avoids deploying malware; uses base64-encoded commands, curl, wget, and shell piping to avoid signatures—detection baseline critical for investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on base64 decoding in command lines, unusual curl/wget with pipe-to-bash patterns, and certutil/bitsadmin used for data transfer. Baseline command patterns per user to detect anomalies.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Persistence via Authorized SSH Keys and Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Investigation leading to extradition suggests detection of persistent backdoors; group uses ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and cron jobs for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for additions to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.ssh/config, /root/.ssh/*, or /etc/cron.d/ via file integrity monitoring. Alert on cron jobs containing reverse shells, curl callbacks, or SSH tunneling.

suggestion.title: Package Registry Credential Exposure via Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'tells you which machine pulled a compromised package'—implies detection of machine identity + package pull correlation. No UC captures machine-to-package mapping or registry authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package-manager process execution (npm, pip, maven, nuget) with source machine identity and registry endpoint. Flag pulls to public registries of packages not in baseline deployment manifest. Compare machine identity claimed in registry pull logs to AD/MDM enrollment records to detect lateral movement or workstation impersonation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Execution Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title implies package installation was detected retroactively ('now tells you')—but no detection for post-installation execution of code from compromised package. Should map to T1203 or T1187.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from package installation directories or by package-manager wrapper processes. Alert on unsigned executables or scripts launched from vendor-standard package cache paths (/node_modules, site-packages, lib/, etc.). Correlate process lineage to timestamp of package pull from IOC'd registry.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Artifact Hash Mismatch in Registry
suggestion.rationale: A 'Secure Registry' feature detecting compromised packages implies cryptographic validation. No UC for hash or signature mismatch detection between published and installed artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare file hashes of installed packages against published hashes in official registries (or signed manifests). suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor splunkd and python processes for anomalous file creation/deletion outside normal SPLUNK_HOME patterns. Alert on rapid sequential file truncations, deletion of config files, or writes to system-critical paths. Correlate timing with unauthorized HTTP POST sequences.

suggestion.title: Missing Authentication on Splunk Admin Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability core: 'missing authentication for critical function'—detection requires endpoint-level auth-bypass monitoring specific to Splunk administrative paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Splunk access logs for /services/*, /admin/*, and /en-US/app/admin paths. Expected: 401 Unauthorized or 302 redirect-to-login for unauthenticated requests. Alert on 200 OK responses to these paths when client IP lacks prior successful authentication or valid session cookie.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Restart and Error Spike
suggestion.rationale: File truncation via sidecar could degrade/stop the service—'truncate arbitrary files' may impact data availability, requiring impact-phase monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar process uptime, restart frequency, and connection error rates. Alert on unexpected service restarts within 5 minutes of suspicious HTTP activity. Check Splunk internal logs for I/O exceptions, file-not-found errors, or permission denials in postgres directories.

suggestion.title: Known Exploited Vulnerability Timeline-Based Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'CISA KEV entry' (actively exploited in wild) with federal patch due-date 2026-06-21—exploitation window requires time-bounded detection urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create high-confidence alert rule active from publication date (2026-06-18) through 60+ days post-patch-due-date (2026-06-21). Match any Splunk Enterprise version against CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability status. Cross-reference with proof-of-concept exploit availability and confirmed-exploitation threat feeds. Escalate to emergency remediation workflow.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—must detect HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints lacking authentication headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically /_internal/postgres or similar URI patterns) from external IPs or lacking valid session tokens and authorization headers. Baseline internal traffic; flag unauthenticated external requests.

suggestion.title: Splunk File Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies capability to 'truncate arbitrary files'—need endpoint detection of file deletion/truncation events correlated with sidecar service process activity on exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file deletion or truncation operations (especially of .conf, .py, encrypted keys, or critical data files) executed by splunkd, postgres, or sidecar processes. Correlate with HTTP access logs showing unauthenticated requests to sidecar endpoints in the preceding seconds. Flag sensitive targets: apps/, default/, var/lib/splunk/, etc/splunk/.

suggestion.title: Splunk Arbitrary File Creation via Unauthenticated Sidecar Request
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'create or truncate arbitrary files through' the endpoint—detect suspicious file creation triggered by unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file creation or write events in system or application directories by splunkd or sidecar processes occurring within 5 seconds of unauthenticated HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints. Prioritize .conf, .py, .sh, and var/ paths. Investigate source IP and request headers.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar on Internet-Facing Asset
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires exposed endpoint reachable from the internet (T1190: Exploit Public-Facing Application)—network-based detection of accessible PostgreSQL sidecar on external-facing Splunk instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for inbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Splunk instances on standard ports (8089, 8000, 8088) from non-corporate/non-approved ASNs probing for PostgreSQL sidecar paths or receiving successful responses (200 HTTP codes). Geographic anomalies in source IPs increase fidelity.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Fingerprinting and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attackers probe for vulnerable versions and sidecar accessibility before exploitation—detect reconnaissance patterns preceding successful file manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequences of HTTP OPTIONS, HEAD, or STATUS requests to sidecar paths followed by POST/PUT requests with file-manipulation payloads. Repeated 404 errors followed by 200 responses on same endpoint warrant escalation as likely exploitation sequence.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—exploit requires HTTP access to sidecar without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (e.g., /sidecar/*, /postgres/*) from external/untrusted networks without authentication headers. Alert on 401/403 followed by 200 responses within short window, or file operation requests (create=, truncate=, write=) lacking authorization.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Attack payload is 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—detectable via file integrity monitoring and audit logs on Splunk instances as impact-phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and truncation events on Splunk Enterprise systems targeting sensitive paths (/etc, /var, system binaries, Splunk config). Correlate timing with preceding unauthenticated sidecar access. Alert if operations originate from sidecar service account or listener processes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'standard asset-exposure hunt' template for this CVE; pipeline should generate network queries to identify exposed Splunk instances regardless of patch status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query firewall/proxy logs for Splunk Enterprise ports (8000 REST, 8089 management, 5432 for sidecar PostgreSQL) visible to untrusted networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20253 presence. Generate unpatched asset list as of federal deadline 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Endpoint Reconnaissance Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation reconnaissance would include HTTP method/parameter enumeration against sidecar; suspicious patterns should precede successful exploit chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP OPTIONS, TRACE, or PROPFIND requests to /sidecar or /postgres endpoints; parameter fuzzing attempts (file=*, truncate=*, create=*); or high-volume 404s on sidecar paths from single source. Alert on any enumeration preceding successful file operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: As a CISA KEV entry with active in-the-wild exploitation, known exploit signatures should be detectable in network and application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy network-based IDS signatures for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation patterns against sidecar endpoints. Monitor WAF logs for POST/GET to /sidecar with file operation parameters or PostgreSQL injection payloads. Alert on any signatures with severity >= high.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Unauthenticated access IS the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TCP/HTTP connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar port (5432 or configured alternate) from external/unexpected sources without valid Splunk auth tokens, session cookies, or TLS client certificates. Whitelist known internal clients; flag all others.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation or Truncation via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the direct impact; file operations outside normal Splunk workflow are abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk service processes (splunkd, PostgreSQL sidecar, associated Python processes) for file creation/deletion/truncation outside whitelisted directories (/opt/splunk/var, /opt/splunk/etc). Alert on writes to /etc, /usr/bin, or Splunk binary directories. Correlate with unauthenticated sidecar access events.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Query Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: PostgreSQL sidecar is the named attack surface. Exploiting missing authentication likely involves injected queries or function calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts to PostgreSQL followed by successful command execution, malformed/obfuscated queries from unauthenticated sessions, or SQL commands targeting file I/O (COPY, file functions). Monitor for unusual privilege escalation patterns in PostgreSQL audit logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise sidecar Port Exposure

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all Splunk Enterprise instances for PostgreSQL sidecar port accessibility from untrusted networks (non-corporate IP ranges, Internet). Cross-reference with CVE-2026-20253 scanner results. Alert on any sidecar port binding to 0.0.0.0 or exposed via public load balancers.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct initial-access surface with no auth requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound traffic to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service ports (typically 5432 or alternate) for connection attempts without valid session tokens. Flag requests originating from untrusted networks or external IPs. Correlate with absence of authenticated Splunk user context.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Deletion from Splunk Sidecar Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Detect unauthorized file operations executed through exploited endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and deletion events originating from Splunk Enterprise service account (splunkd) outside normal config/data paths. Flag writes to system-critical directories (Windows: System32, Program Files; Linux: /etc, /root, /bin). Detect rapid file truncations or deletion cascades.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Service Restart Following Endpoint Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: exploitation via endpoint can trigger service instability. Detect crash/restart patterns post-attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected Splunk sidecar/PostgreSQL service process termination or restart with prior suspicious network activity to service endpoints. Flag error log entries mentioning 'critical function' failures or authentication errors in same time window.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Splunk Enterprise Instance (Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and vulnerability requires network access. Identify publicly routable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise listening sockets bound to public IPs or accessible from untrusted CIDR ranges. Flag instances not fronted by VPN/proxy requiring authentication. Cross-reference CMDB to identify unintended external exposure.

suggestion.title: Configuration Tampering: Sidecar Auth Bypass or Permission Escalation
suggestion.rationale: File creation capability implies potential auth config modification. Detect suspicious changes to endpoint security or service permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk configuration directories for modifications to auth settings, ACLs, or sidecar endpoint configs. Flag file ownership/permission changes on sidecar-related binaries or config files. Alert on service account privilege changes.

suggestion.title: StealC/Amadey Process Execution and DLL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses infostealer execution; infostealers use process hollowing and DLL injection to evade detection and establish persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with suspicious parent (winrar, 7zip, email clients) launching legitimate executables (svchost, rundll32) that subsequently load unsigned or mismatched DLLs. StealC typically injects into explorer.exe or svchost; look for abnormal DLL import sequences.

suggestion.title: Infostealer Credential and Token Harvesting from Browsers
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes credential theft and token exfiltration—core function of StealC and Amadey targeting browser stored passwords, cookies, autofill data, and OAuth tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-browser processes (rundll32, powershell, cmd) reading or accessing browser credential storage paths (%APPDATA%\..\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data, %APPDATA%\..\Roaming\Mozilla\Firefox). StealC typically spawns threads that target Chrome SQLite databases and Firefox profile data.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Software Access by Suspicious Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'cybercrime services'—infostealers target crypto wallets and exchange credentials; StealC and Amadey enumerate installed wallet applications and exfiltrate seed phrases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawning child processes that enumerate or access known crypto-wallet paths or registry hives (Ledger, Trezor, MetaMask, Exodus installation/config directories). Correlate with file access to wallet.dat or similar persistence files.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP/HTTPS Exfiltration to Unnamed or Free Hosting Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes infrastructure used to deliver and command infostealers; StealC/Amadey beacon to attacker-controlled C2 servers to upload harvested credentials and browser data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS POST requests from suspicious processes (rundll32, wscript, powershell) to newly registered or bulletproof hosting domains with high reputation risk scores. StealC C2 endpoints often use dynamic DNS and minimal SSL certificate history.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: StealC Anti-Analysis Techniques (VM/Sandbox Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Infostealers deploy anti-analysis checks; article likely discusses evasion tactics used by these families to avoid researcher/sandbox analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious API calls or registry queries indicative of VM/sandbox detection (CPUID checks, WMI queries for hypervisor presence, checks for debuggers). StealC queries registry keys like HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\disk and accesses WMI classes.

suggestion.title: Trojan Downloader Activity Preceding Infostealer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'cybercrime services that deliver them'—implies multi-stage delivery chain where droppers or downloaders precede StealC/Amadey execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email delivery artifacts (MSG parser, Outlook temp files) with suspicious download activity (certutil.exe, BITSAdmin, curl, wget) followed by execution of newly written executables in temp directories. Look for parent-child chains: email client → downloader → unpacked infostealer.
