suggestion.title: Unauthenticated File Upload to SP Page Builder Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files'—this is the primary attack vector and should trigger detection on POST/PUT requests to known upload paths without authentication headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to SP Page Builder upload directories (typically /components/com_sppagebuilder/uploads or variants) from unauthenticated sessions. Flag any successful 200-201 responses. Expected false positives: legitimate content editors uploading images; mitigate by whitelisting known admin IP ranges.

suggestion.title: PHP or Executable File Upload Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type' and 'upload and execution of PHP code'—should detect upload of .php, .phtml, .php3, .php4, .php5, or other executable extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect uploaded file names or Content-Type headers in HTTP requests to upload endpoints for executable extensions (.php, .phtml, .php3-5, .shtml) or MIME type mismatches (e.g., image/jpeg header on .php file). Alert on any successful upload of these file types.

suggestion.title: Execution of Recently Uploaded PHP File
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'resulting in the upload and execution of PHP code'—should correlate file writes to upload directories with subsequent PHP script execution or process spawning from the web root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP/CGI process execution (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with command line or working directory pointing to the SP Page Builder upload directory, especially within 1–10 seconds of a file write event in that same directory. Flag processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash from the web process context.

suggestion.title: Rapid or Repeated Upload Requests to SP Page Builder
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated upload capability—attackers will probe and iterate; should detect brute-force or scanning patterns on upload endpoints as early indicator of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Count POST/PUT requests to SP Page Builder upload endpoints per source IP per 5-minute window. Alert if count exceeds 10 requests or if multiple unique file names are uploaded in rapid succession from a single source, especially if followed by 4xx errors (file type rejection attempts).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Content-Type or Filename Encoding in Upload Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'unrestricted upload'—attackers will use encoding tricks (double extension, null bytes, MIME type confusion) to bypass filters; detection should flag obfuscated file names or mismatched MIME types.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect upload POST requests with file name encoding anomalies (null bytes, %00, double extensions like .php.jpg, base64-encoded names, or Content-Type headers that mismatch the declared file extension). Flag especially if Content-Type is generic (application/octet-stream) for files claiming .php or similar.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48908 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48908 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and is a CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild). Pipeline generated no UC for the foundational detection method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-48908 (JoomShaper SP Page Builder), especially on internet-facing systems. Cross-reference against patch inventory to distinguish true vulnerabilities from scanner false negatives. Patch due-date: 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated File Upload to JoomShaper Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'allows unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files'. This is the core initial-access vector (T1190) that pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/PUT requests to JoomShaper SP Page Builder upload endpoints from unauthenticated sources. Baseline: authenticated admins only. Flag rapid uploads, uploads from external/untrusted IPs, or upload attempts to paths not normally used.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Uploaded Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'results in the upload and execution of PHP code'. Pipeline failed to operationalize the execution phase of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of PHP scripts from temporary, cache, or media upload directories. Alert on unusual process spawning from web server context or PHP include/require statements referencing user-controlled file paths.

suggestion.title: JoomShaper SP Page Builder Asset Inventory and Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch-due 2026-07-10; article emphasizes patch lag as 'silent killer' and auditors will demand remediation status. Pipeline skipped inventory as foundational hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all systems running JoomShaper SP Page Builder, especially internet-exposed instances. Categorize by: (a) patched vs. unpatched, (b) internet-exposed vs. internal-only. Prioritize unpatched + internet-exposed for remediation by federal due-date.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Outbound Activity from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: After successful PHP code upload, attacker achieves RCE within web server context. Pipeline generated no post-exploitation C2 or data-exfiltration detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Following successful file upload to JoomShaper endpoint, alert on unusual outbound connections from web server process (www-data, apache, iis apppool), unexpected DNS queries, or traffic to known C2 indicators.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Activity Against JoomShaper Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article implies unauthenticated exploitation, but attackers typically enumerate endpoints first. Pipeline should detect failed auth attempts and upload-path probing preceding actual exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Spike in failed login attempts to JoomShaper admin paths (/administrator, /index.php?option=com_login) or repeated probes to upload endpoints. Correlate failed auth + unauthenticated upload attempts from same source IP as indicator of active exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Malicious Software Download from SEO-Poisoned Site
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'SEO-Poisoned Software Sites' as initial vector. Pipeline missed detection for downloads originating from lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of software installers (exe, msi, zip) from domains registered recently or with typosquatting patterns. Correlate parent process (browser) with file write to Downloads folder followed by execution.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Abuse for Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Abuse ScreenConnect to Deploy AsyncRAT' but pipeline generated no execution-phase detection. ScreenConnect is Connectwise legitimate software; detect anomalous process spawning or registry modifications under its context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ScreenConnect.exe or its child processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unknown binaries. Flag modifications to registry HKCU\Software by ScreenConnect service context.

suggestion.title: AsyncRAT Process Execution and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Malware family name in title but zero indicators produced. AsyncRAT is known for process injection, registry persistence (Run keys), and HTTP/HTTPS C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AsyncRAT signatures: process names like 'rat.exe', 'client.exe'; registry writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run; HTTP POST to unusual ports; parent-child process chains with uncommon combinations.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence - AsyncRAT Autostart Configuration
suggestion.rationale: AsyncRAT family commonly establishes Run key persistence. Article describes malware deployment but pipeline missed persistence-phase coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and RunOnce for registry values pointing to executables in %temp%, %appdata%, or user Downloads. Flag entries with randomized names + uncommon binary locations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Non-Interactive Process
suggestion.rationale: AsyncRAT frequently uses PowerShell for secondary payload delivery and C2 communication. Pipeline missed command-execution indicators implied by 'Deploy AsyncRAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe spawned by non-shell parents (services, browsers, msiexec) with command-line flags -nop (no profile), -enc (encoded), or -c (command). Inspect for Base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Communication on Non-Standard Ports
suggestion.rationale: AsyncRAT C2 often communicates over ports 80/443 or randomized high ports. No network-based detections in pipeline output despite C2 being central to attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate newly-launched suspicious processes with outbound HTTP/HTTPS to IPs (not hostnames) on ports 8080, 8443, 3389 variants, or rapid port-scanning. Flag if destination IP is not in known CDN/cloud ranges.

suggestion.title: Detect JoomShaper SP Page Builder Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unrestricted upload affecting this product; defenders must locate exposed instances first. Article explicitly references 'canonical Splunk SPL' asset-exposure template but pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to /components/com_sppagebuilder/ paths in proxy/firewall logs. Flag responses with HTTP 200 and typical joomla/page-builder response markers. Correlate with port scans or Shodan data to identify exposed Joomla instances running the vulnerable plugin.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated File Upload to SP Page Builder
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files'—no detection for the upload POST requests themselves, which is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST with multipart/form-data to /components/com_sppagebuilder/upload* or equivalent endpoints from unauthenticated sources. Baseline legitimate upload patterns and flag deviations (rapid uploads, oversized payloads, double-extension files like shell.php.jpg).

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious PHP File Creation in SP Page Builder Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'execution of PHP code' following upload; file-system detection must catch .php/.phtml files created in the plugin directory post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /components/com_sppagebuilder/ recursively for new .php, .phtml, .phar, .shtml files created by web-server processes (www-data, apache, tomcat). Alert if creation correlates with recent proxy-logged uploads to the component.

suggestion.title: Detect Web Shell Execution in SP Page Builder Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'upload and execution of PHP code' but pipeline missed the execution-phase detection. Uploaded shells will exhibit command-execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to /components/com_sppagebuilder/*.php with command-execution patterns: query strings containing cmd=, system=, exec=, or shell metacharacters. Alert on web-application process spawning child shells (bash, sh, powershell) with arguments matching request parameters.

suggestion.title: Detect Path Traversal or Double-Extension Bypass in Upload
suggestion.rationale: Common evasion technique for upload restrictions; article does not specify validation but vulnerability description implies lack of filtering that could enable ../ or double-extension attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST uploads containing ../, null bytes (%00), double extensions (.php.jpg, .phtml.txt), or mixed-case variants (.pHP) in the filename parameter. WAF/proxy rules should block before application processing.

suggestion.title: Inventory Joomla Instances and SP Page Builder Versions
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-48908 affects specific product versions; fingerprinting via HTTP headers or admin panels helps scope vulnerable assets for patch prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Perform HTTP HEAD/GET to /administrator/ or /index.php?option=com_sppagebuilder and extract version strings from response headers, HTML comments, or version.php files. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-48908 affected versions to identify patch-required assets.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Match: CVE-2026-48908 (JoomShaper SP Page Builder)
suggestion.rationale: Article instructs substitution of CVE-2026-48908 into standard asset-exposure template. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite explicit template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner reports for CVE-2026-48908 matches against JoomShaper SP Page Builder installations. Cross-reference with asset exposure (public-facing, internet-routable) to prioritize remediation by federal due date 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated File Upload to JoomShaper SP Page Builder
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary files.' This is the core attack vector; pipeline missed it despite explicit attack description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests to JoomShaper SP Page Builder upload endpoints (e.g., /upload, /media, /components/com_sppagebuilder/upload) from unauthenticated sessions (no valid session token). Flag requests with suspicious file extensions (.php, .phtml, .exe, .sh, .jsp).

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution Post-File Upload (Web Shell Activity)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states upload 'ultimately resulting in...execution of PHP code.' Detection for post-upload execution is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web requests immediately following successful file uploads to JoomShaper, especially requests that trigger PHP execution (GET/POST to uploaded file paths, requests with suspicious query parameters like ?cmd=, ?execute=, or base64-encoded payloads). Look for 200 responses to newly-created .php files in upload directories.

suggestion.title: JoomShaper SP Page Builder Exposed Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article implies public-facing exploitation risk. Asset discovery detection should identify exposed JoomShaper installations before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint JoomShaper SP Page Builder web applications via characteristic HTTP headers, HTML comments, or URL patterns (e.g., /components/com_sppagebuilder, jQuery.sppagebuilder JavaScript library). Cross-reference with public-facing firewall rules and internet-routable CIDR blocks. Match against known vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Bypass of Authentication/Authorization on File Upload Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated users' to upload; this is an auth bypass. Expected detection for unauthorized access is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file upload requests (multipart/form-data POST) to JoomShaper upload endpoints where request lacks valid authentication (no session cookie, bearer token, or authenticated user ID). Baseline upload endpoint access—flag significant deviation from expected authentication posture.

suggestion.title: Android Banking Malware Execution via Masqueraded APK
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'packages Android Bank Fraud'—clear reference to malicious APK delivery and execution on Android devices targeting financial institutions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of obfuscated (T1406) processes spawned from legitimate banking app package names (T1444 masquerading). Detect service execution (T1409) from non-standard app paths and correlate with Telegram network communication.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot C2 Communication for Malware Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Telegram Rental Service'—Telegram bots serve as both distribution channel and C2 command infrastructure for the RedWing MaaS operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Android processes establishing encrypted connections to Telegram API endpoints (T1071 application layer protocol). Alert on encrypted exfiltration to Telegram (T1041) carrying banking credentials or transaction data. Flag Telegram bot interaction patterns consistent with C2 beaconing rather than user-initiated messaging.

suggestion.title: Input Capture from Compromised Banking Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Bank Fraud' as objective—implies credential harvesting from banking apps via input capture (keylogging, clipboard monitoring) on Android.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-system Android apps installing input capture hooks (T1056) targeting banking app UI layers. Monitor for credential caching bypasses and defense evasion (T1411) that disable OS-level banking app protections. Correlate with suspicious Telegram exfiltration channels.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Distribution and Installation from Telegram
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Telegram Rental Service' model—users download and install trojanized banking APKs through Telegram rather than official app stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK downloads via Telegram messenger application (T1195 supply chain compromise via unofficial distribution). Detect installations from unknown sources with mismatched or invalid signing certificates. Flag APKs masquerading (T1444) as legitimate banking apps with obfuscated manifests or suspicious embedded permissions (location, SMS, contacts).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Financial Transactions from Compromised Banking Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Bank Fraud' end goal; detection of unauthorized transactions initiated from devices with confirmed input capture and Telegram exfiltration activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential theft indicators (input capture from banking apps via T1056) with anomalous banking transactions: rapid-succession transfers to new payees, unusual transaction amounts/times, transactions initiated from rooted/modified device fingerprints, or app version mismatches.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Exploitation by Android Banking Malware
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans often exploit Android vulnerabilities to achieve root access, escape sandbox restrictions, and persist across updates—article's critical severity suggests advanced exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation of known Android privilege escalation CVEs (T1407) triggered by non-system APKs, particularly those with banking-related package names. Monitor for su/sudo execution, kernel module loading, or SELinux policy modifications stemming from banking app child processes.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider RDP Lateral Movement — Anomalous Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article title and Scattered Spider's known TTPs: group is notorious for credential harvesting and RDP abuse for lateral movement. No use cases generated despite this being the actor's signature technique. Article mentions FBI trace via Windows identifiers, implying extensive RDP/lateral movement telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed RDP logon attempts followed by successful logon from anomalous source IP or user-agent, especially where source lacks endpoint telemetry. Alert on Pass-the-Hash indicators (NTLM relay, Kerberos ticket reuse) across multiple systems in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Windows Device ID Enumeration and Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Windows Device ID Helped FBI Trace' — this is the forensic mechanism that led to attribution. Pipeline did not generate any detection hypothesis around WDID collection or abnormal queries for device identifiers that would indicate attacker reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes querying Windows registry paths containing device-specific identifiers (MachineGuid, ProductId, DeviceId) via WMI, registry APIs, or command-line tools. Flag batch enumeration of device IDs across multiple systems, especially from interactive accounts with no legitimate admin role.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing — Scattered Spider Ingress
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider's initial access vector is phishing/credential harvesting (T1598/T1187). Article mentions court filing about tracing, implying evidence chain starting from initial compromise. No use case generated for detecting credential harvesting or initial phishing payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing email delivery with credential entry into attacker infrastructure (inferred from C2 callbacks or lateral movement source IPs). Alert on creation of 2FA bypass codes or password manager modifications shortly after phishing click. Monitor for suspicious email forwarding rules or recovery email changes post-compromise.

suggestion.title: External Remote Service Exploitation — VPN/Citrix Abuse
suggestion.rationale: FBI tracing implies attacker maintained persistence via externally-accessible services. Scattered Spider frequently abuses VPN, Citrix, and RDP gateways. Article provides no context on entry point, but law enforcement recovery suggests multiple access paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN/Citrix logons from residential IP ranges, unusual geographic locations, or IPs associated with credential stuffing infrastructure. Alert on failed authentication attempts followed by successful logon using same IP within hours. Monitor for VPN client process injection or memory modification.

suggestion.title: Pass-the-Hash / Ticket Detection — Token Reuse Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider's persistence mechanism relies on stolen NTLM hashes and Kerberos tickets. FBI identification via Windows Device ID suggests forensic recovery of lateral movement chains. Pipeline missed core evasion technique that enabled dwell time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NTLM Type-3 authentication messages originating from non-workstation processes (e.g., rundll32, powershell). Alert on Kerberos TGT requests from non-interactive logon sessions or for krbtgt-modified tickets. Correlate SMB session creation with absence of corresponding network authentication events.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land Command Execution — Defense Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider minimizes malware footprint via LOLBin abuse. Court filing implies detailed forensic reconstruction; this requires telemetry on command-line tool execution (certutil, bitsadmin, etc.). Pipeline generated no defense-evasion use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect certutil, bitsadmin, or rundll32 spawned from explorer.exe, cmd.exe, or PowerShell with network arguments. Flag encoded payloads (base64, hex) in command lines. Alert on LOLBin process creation with unusual parent process (e.g., svchost, lsass).

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Credential Harvesting via Phishing & Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Scattered Spider's documented signature TTP is initial compromise through phishing and social engineering to steal credentials; article title references criminal hacking charges implying orchestrated intrusions beginning with credential theft
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails with urgency-driven messaging, password-reset requests, or fake MFA prompts. Correlate email clicks on malicious URLs with subsequent failed authentication attempts or credential-submission POST requests from same user. Flag campaigns targeting privileged users.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Lateral Movement via Valid Compromised Credentials
suggestion.rationale: After credential compromise, Scattered Spider moves laterally using valid accounts; article references widespread hacking charges indicating multi-system unauthorized access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag multiple failed RDP/SSH login attempts from single IP followed by successful logon within 1 hour. Detect successful logons to high-value hosts from atypical source IPs or geographically impossible locations. Correlate VPN access with immediate lateral movement to internal systems.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Post-Compromise Active Directory Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attacker requires user/group enumeration to identify targets for privilege escalation and data exfiltration; reconnaissance is consistent with sustained intrusion campaign described in extradition case
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid LDAP queries, Get-ADUser, net user, or dsquery commands targeting multiple users/groups from single source within 10 minutes. Flag execution of AD enumeration tools (AdFind, BloodHound) from user workstations outside normal business hours.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Data Exfiltration via VPN or Proxy Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Criminal extradition charges directly imply significant data theft; Scattered Spider uses compromised credentials to maintain VPN/proxy access for persistent exfiltration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN/proxy sessions for anomalous egress: large file transfers to consumer cloud storage (Mega, ProtonDrive), unusual destinations, or protocol anomalies (HTTPS tunnels for non-web protocols). Correlate with valid-account logons from residential/VPS IP space and after-hours activity.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: Privilege Escalation via Valid Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Once gaining initial foothold via compromised user credentials, attacker escalates to domain-admin or service accounts to enable broader system compromise described in indictment
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logons to service accounts or domain-admin groups from non-standard source IPs or from normal user workstations. Flag suspicious use of RunAs, sudo, or service-account credentials. Monitor for account additions to high-privileged groups outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider: VPN/Proxy Access Pattern Anomalies Indicating Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attacker gains persistent foothold by maintaining VPN access using stolen credentials; geographic anomalies and time-of-access patterns differ sharply from legitimate user behavior
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify VPN logons from geographically impossible locations (user in two distant cities <30 min apart). Detect logons from residential ISPs or datacenter IP space for business users. Flag VPN access outside normal business hours followed by internal lateral movement.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Suspicious Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—post-exploitation detection must watch for child processes spawned unexpectedly from the ColdFusion runtime (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh from cfusion.exe or jrun.exe).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ProcessCreationEvents where ParentImage contains 'coldfusion' or 'cfusion' or 'jrun', looking for unexpected child processes (cmd, powershell, bash, etc.). ColdFusion should not spawn interactive shells under normal operation. Alert on any instances, as they indicate post-exploitation code execution.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion HTTP Path Traversal Patterns
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability is explicitly a 'path traversal' type—detection should look for HTTP requests with traversal sequences (../, ..\ encoding variants) targeting ColdFusion endpoints on port 8500 or via web roots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests with path traversal payloads (../, %2e%2e/, ..\) in the URI or POST body targeting ColdFusion CFML files, CFAdmin endpoints, or known ColdFusion web roots. Combine with user-agent anomalies or POST requests with unusual Content-Length to catch active exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Scanner/PoC Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active exploitation in the wild—network detection should identify fingerprint probes (scanner, Metasploit, public PoC requests) attempting to confirm ColdFusion vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests with known PoC/scanner signatures for CVE-2026-48282 (specific request paths, User-Agent strings from public PoC repos, or timing/volume patterns consistent with exploitation attempts). Reference Shodan/Censys query patterns for exposed ColdFusion to identify which instances are Internet-facing.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify affected versions; however, CISA KEV entry + patch-due date 2026-07-10 means urgent scanning required. Detection use case should ensure inventory of all ColdFusion instances and versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all external-facing web servers for ColdFusion instances (port 8500, known CF URLs, response headers). Cross-reference identified versions against CISA KEV advisory to confirm which instances are vulnerable; alert on any unpatched instances exposed to the Internet by the patch-due date.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Outbound C2 Activity Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE from path traversal may lead to C2 callbacks. Monitor ColdFusion process network behavior to detect post-exploitation callbacks or lateral-movement activity (DNS, HTTP/HTTPS connections to suspicious hosts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ColdFusion process ID (cfusion.exe, jrun.exe) with outbound connections to non-whitelisted destinations. Flag any DNS queries from ColdFusion process, HTTP/HTTPS connections to unknown hosts, or anomalous data exfiltration. Compare against baseline ColdFusion connectivity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48282 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and specifies federal remediation due date 2026-07-10. This is the canonical asset-exposure hunt the article references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner or patch management system detecting CVE-2026-48282 (Adobe ColdFusion) on internet-facing systems. Cross-correlate patch status against federal deadline; escalate unpatched instances on public-facing assets to critical priority.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal HTTP Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability'; traversal payloads are detectable in HTTP access logs, WAF logs, and IIS logs before successful code execution. Patterns like '../', '..\', URL-encoded variants are characteristic indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP requests to ColdFusion endpoints for path traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e, etc.) combined with common ColdFusion file paths (cfusion, coldfusion, administrator, modules). Alert on repeated patterns indicating scanning or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from ColdFusion Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability causes 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'; successful exploitation manifests as child processes spawned from cfusion.exe or coldfusion.exe containers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected child process creation under ColdFusion processes (cfusion.exe, coldfusion.exe, cfserver.exe), especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or spawning scheduled-task infrastructure. Baseline normal process trees; alert on deviations within 60 minutes post-traversal HTTP attempts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Configuration File Access via Path Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal vulnerability allows reading files outside application web root; successful exploitation yields configuration disclosures (web.config, database credentials, encryption keys).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion access logs for successful HTTP responses (200/304) to path-traversal requests targeting system directories or config files outside the app root. Correlate with process file-read events for coldfusion.exe accessing sensitive config paths.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal in Web Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'path traversal vulnerability' is the attack vector. T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is the direct mapping. No UC generated for detecting traversal patterns in HTTP logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion web application access logs for directory traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, null bytes) in URI paths or query parameters. Look for 400/403 errors followed by successful requests indicating exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Process Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'—implies process spawn or code injection from web service account. No execution-phase UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation events where parent process is ColdFusion (cfusion.exe/coldfusion) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or unusual child processes. This indicates post-exploitation command execution.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal explicitly mentioned; likely involves file system access outside intended directory structure. No file access detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file read/write events from ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe) accessing files outside its application directory, web root, or system paths (e.g., C:\Windows, C:\Program Files outside ColdFusion install). Baseline normal behavior first.

suggestion.title: Adobe ColdFusion Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-10' and emphasizes patch lag as 'the silent killer.' No inventory or compliance detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Adobe ColdFusion installations. Flag any version prior to patched build for CVE-2026-48282. Cross-reference with public-facing web servers via network scan data or firewall rules.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Error/Exception Logging Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal attacks typically generate application errors (file not found, access denied, invalid path exceptions). No log aggregation rule for ColdFusion error patterns generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion error logs for repeated file-not-found or access-denied exceptions correlated with HTTP 4xx responses. Traversal attempts often produce distinctive exception stacks; alert on clusters within short time windows from single source IP.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public-Facing Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'public-facing application' in KEV context and states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited.' Baseline asset-exposure hunt is mandatory first step for T1190. Article phrase: 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ColdFusion instances accessible on standard web ports (80, 443, 8500, 8501) from external/untrusted networks. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-48282 status. Flag unpatched instances against federal due-date 2026-07-10.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal Exploitation Attempts Against ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Exploit vector explicitly stated as 'path traversal vulnerability' — HTTP detection logic must target traversal indicators in request URIs. Article phrase: 'Adobe ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for path traversal patterns (../, ..\, %2e%2e, unicode encodings) targeting ColdFusion application paths (/cfadmin, /cfusion, /CFIDE). Prioritize external sources. Alert on successful responses (200, 302) indicating traversal succeeded.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution Post-Exploitation from ColdFusion
suggestion.rationale: Impact explicitly stated as 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user' — post-compromise signal requires process execution detection from ColdFusion service runtime. Article phrase: 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by ColdFusion runtime (java.exe, cfscript.exe) executing cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or script interpreters with anomalous prevalence. Correlate with preceding HTTP path traversal attempts. Flag file creation in system directories from ColdFusion service.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states CVE should be substituted into template. Pipeline generated no asset-inventory or version-detection UC. Phrase: 'Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on hosts running known-vulnerable Adobe ColdFusion versions (scanner match CVE-2026-48282). Correlate with network-exposure assessment to identify public-facing ColdFusion instances. Track application version strings in HTTP headers (Server: ColdFusion) and diagnostic endpoints.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'path traversal vulnerability' leading to RCE but no detection UC for the traversal payload itself. This is the attack vector—exploitation happens before RCE symptoms appear.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to ColdFusion application paths containing path-traversal sequences (../, ..\, %2e%2e%2f, %252e%252e%252f) or common ColdFusion administrative/diagnostic endpoints (cfide/, CFIDE/, Administrator/). Flag requests with 200/302 responses following traversal payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-ColdFusion RCE Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Pipeline should detect post-exploitation command execution following successful exploitation. Phrase: 'arbitrary code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned from ColdFusion/ColdFusion.exe (cfusion.exe, java.exe parent). Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripting engines (cscript.exe, wscript.exe) launched from web application context or SYSTEM user with web-app parent. Correlate timing with recent ColdFusion requests to suspected path-traversal payloads.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Compliance Remediation Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal due-date dates' and 'patch lag is the silent killer' with explicit deadline 2026-07-10. Pipeline should generate compliance-tracking UC for known-exploited vuln with federal remediation deadlines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference CISA KEV list against vulnerability scanner results and patch-audit data. Flag any host running unpatched ColdFusion with CVE-2026-48282 and alert SOC/asset owners with federal due-date context. Track remediation progress toward 2026-07-10 deadline.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable ColdFusion Version Detection via Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-48282 is actively exploited; baseline UC for any CISA KEV entry is flagging vulnerable versions. Article: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by the published due date'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ColdFusion installations with version < patched baseline. Cross-correlate vulnerability scan results against asset inventory for exposed instances (public-facing ColdFusion apps). Pivot on CVE-2026-48282 presence.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'path traversal vulnerability'; this is the attack vector. Article: 'Adobe ColdFusion contains a path traversal vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for path traversal payloads in ColdFusion access logs: sequences of `../`, `..\`, URL-encoded variants (`%2e%2e/`), or directory traversal keywords (e.g., `/../../../../`, `/cf_root/`, `/windows/`). Correlate with ColdFusion process access to sensitive files outside the app root.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: ColdFusion RCE via Shell Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution'; this is the execution phase after path traversal succeeds. Article: 'arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion process (cfusion.exe, jrun, etc.) spawning unusual child processes: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, cscript.exe, wscript.exe. Baseline ColdFusion legitimate child processes; flag anomalies. Enriched: correlate with path traversal attempts in preceding 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion File System Access Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal to RCE typically involves reading/writing outside normal app directories. Article: 'path traversal vulnerability...arbitrary code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ColdFusion process accessing files outside designated app directory (e.g., C:\Windows\, C:\Program Files\, system root). High-confidence signal: reads to sensitive system files (SAM, LSASS, boot.ini) or writes to startup folders, Global Assembly Cache, or Windows\System32 via ColdFusion context.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence Check Post-ColdFusion Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary code execution is commonly followed by persistence via web shell deployment to ColdFusion app directory. Article: 'arbitrary code execution'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious CFML files (.cfm, .cfc) created in ColdFusion app directories with recent modification timestamps aligned to exploitation attempts. Check ownership, permissions, and content for suspicious tags (cfexecute, cfdirectory, cffile write). Baseline legitimate CFML deployments.

suggestion.title: Data Integrity Alert: CVE Title/Body Mismatch

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated data quality check: verify CVE ID in article title matches body. Flag mismatches for manual triage. This article should either be split (separate title/articles per CVE) or corrected. Downstream consumers (analysts, SOC) would be misled by conflicting vulnerability metadata.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion instances for HTTP requests containing path-traversal patterns (../ sequences, URL-encoded variants %2e%2e) in URI paths. Flag requests to known ColdFusion admin or file-access endpoints combined with traversal syntax.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Post-Exploitation Code Execution

Monitor for child processes spawned from ColdFusion runtime (cfusion.exe, java.exe in ColdFusion context) with suspicious command lines (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe), particularly with no user context matching normal application behavior.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Instance Exposure Inventory

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Admin Console or File-Access Endpoint Targeting

Log 404s and 200s; successful access to sensitive paths post-traversal may return files outside intended directory.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Unexpected File Read or Directory Traversal in Logs

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion service account (usually NETWORK SERVICE or dedicated user) for abnormal file-read activity outside typical application directories. Flag access to /windows/system32, /etc, or configuration files outside sandboxed ColdFusion install paths.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Public Exposure Detection

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48282 Vulnerability Scanner Detection

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Path Traversal Exploit Attempts in Web Logs

suggestion.title: Detect machines pulling from untrusted or compromised package registries

Flag machines with no prior registry access history suddenly pulling packages, or pulls of packages flagged as malicious/compromised by threat intel feeds. Correlate timing and package names across the fleet.

Flag execution of interpreters, shells, curl, powershell, or file-modification tools spawned from package installation directories or by the package manager process seconds after install.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthorized or suspicious edits to dependency manifests

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor edits to package manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml, Gemfile.lock, packages.config, etc.). Flag additions of packages not on org's approved list, unexpected version downgrades, or dependencies pulled from private/unknown registries. Alert on manifests edited by non-developer accounts or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawn from ColdFusion Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could lead to arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user.' Post-exploitation execution detection is critical for response. Phrase: 'arbitrary code execution'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when ColdFusion processes (cfusion.exe, jrunsvc.exe) spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or network tools (bitsadmin, curl, wget). Establish baseline of legitimate administrative spawns; flag anomalies occurring after unsuccessful HTTP probes to the same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Unpatched ColdFusion Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due date is 2026-07-10. Must identify exposed ColdFusion instances running vulnerable versions before exploitation window closes. Phrase: 'public-facing application'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner findings for Adobe ColdFusion products. Filter to instances with exposure (internet-routable, low network segmentation). Alert on any unpatched instances; escalate if accessible from untrusted networks within 72 hours of 2026-07-10 patch deadline.

suggestion.title: ColdFusion Error-Page Directory Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Path traversal vulnerabilities often leak filesystem paths via error responses. Attackers probe for directory structures to refine exploits. Phrase: 'path traversal vulnerability'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ColdFusion web server responses for HTTP 400/404/500 errors containing filesystem paths (e.g., 'C:\ColdFusion\wwwroot\...'). Correlate repeated path-traversal probe patterns (same source, incrementing traversal depth or target paths) with scanning intent.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Repo-Server Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unpatched Argo CD Repo-Server Flaw' as attack vector enabling cluster takeover. Pipeline missed encoding exploit pattern detection against the repo-server HTTP interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Argo CD repo-server endpoints for HTTP requests with anomalous payloads, path traversal, or serialization attack signatures. Flag 4xx→5xx transitions or timeouts preceded by binary/encoded request bodies. Correlate with repo-server process errors.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Kubernetes API Over-Permission
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw 'Could Let Attackers Take Over Kubernetes Clusters'—implies privilege escalation from repo-server context to cluster-admin or equivalent RBAC roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RBAC role bindings or service account tokens originating from Argo CD namespace that grant cluster-admin or wildcard permissions post-infection. Watch for create_binding, patch_rbac, or assume_role calls from Argo CD-controlled identities within 1h of repo-server crash/restart.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Argo CD Application Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Compromised repo-server can deploy arbitrary workloads to managed clusters. Article implies attacker control of deployment pipeline; should detect sudden application manifests outside normal CI/CD rhythm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Argo CD for Application CRD creates/updates with image digests not matching approved registries, or Git commit SHAs that skip branch protection/PR review. Flag deployments originating from repo-server service account after detected compromise window.

suggestion.title: Repository Credential Exfiltration via Repo-Server
suggestion.rationale: Repo-server stores credentials for private Git repositories. Unpatched RCE likely enables attacker to enumerate or export stored SSH keys, deploy tokens, or credentials for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file access or environment variable enumeration of paths like /etc/argo-cd/ssh or mounted secret volumes. Alert on base64 decoding of Argo Secret resources, kubectl exec into repo-server pod, or mass listing of Secret objects by the repo-server identity.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Repo-Server Process Anomaly & Lateral Cluster Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploited repo-server will attempt to move laterally within cluster. Article title mentions 'take over Kubernetes Clusters' (plural), suggesting lateral propagation to other clusters managed by same Argo instance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repo-server pod for spawned child processes (shell, curl, kubectl, git clone), outbound connections to other cluster API servers, or cross-cluster kubeconfig access. Flag kubectl contexts switched or API credentials sourced from mounted /root/.kube or KUBECONFIG envvar.

suggestion.title: Argo CD Repo-Server Container Escape or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies full cluster control; repo-server runs in container. Must detect kernel exploit, seccomp bypass, or cgroup escape attempts to achieve host-level or cluster-admin privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ptrace syscalls, /proc/sys/kernel manipulation, cgroup mount attempts, or kernel module loading from repo-server container. Alert on execution of known CVE exploit payloads (e.g., CVE-2024-XXXXX PoC binaries) or elevation to root within container namespace.
